title: Feasibility, Compliance, and Immune Response to an Intensified Trimodal Prehabilitation Program during Total Neoadjuvant and Perioperative Treatment for Patients with Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (PreReC-Study)
summary: This is a prospective randomized, controlled, multi-center trial. During a total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) and as prehabilitation for a subseuent minimally invasive rectal resection, patients with an adenocarcinoma of the middle and lower rectum without distant metastasis (locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC)) receive an intensified trimodal program including physical exercise, psycho-oncological care and nutritional counseling. Aim of the study is to gain knowledge about feasibility, compliance and immune response to this trimodal prehabilitation program.

interventions.name: total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) + trimodal prehabilitation programm

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Histologically confirmed LARC without distant metastasis with intended nRCT and planned minimally invasive (robotic or laparo-scopic), continence-preserving partial or total mesorectal excision and intended adjuvant therapy after surgery

• Aged 18 – 85 years

• Physical and cognitive ability to perform physical exercise and participate in psycho-oncological treatment at the investigator’s discretion. 
• Physical and cognitive ability to handle digital sources and participate in video conferences. 

• The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
• Rectal cancer without intended total neoadjuvant treatment (TNT) 

• Stage IV rectal cancer

• Current or planned therapy with antibodies or other chemotherapeutic agents except chemotherapy agents of any TNT regime

• Subjects without the cognitive premises to follow psycho-oncological interventions at the investigator’s discretion 

• Subjects without legal capacity who are unable to understand the nature, scope, significance, and consequences of this clinical trial at the investigator’s discretion

• Subjects with a physical or psychiatric condition which at the investigator’s discretion may put the subject at risk, may confound the trial results, or may interfere with the subject’s participation in this clinical trial

• Subjects with previous open abdominal surgeries (exception: appendectomy, cholecystectomy, hysterectomy, adnexectomy)

• Simultaneous participation in another clinical trial, or participation in a clinical trial taking an investigational product, up to 30 days prior to participation in that clinical trial 

• Impossibility to use video calling platforms

• Known or persistent abuse of medication, drugs or alcohol at the investigator’s discretion
